problem: LLM-based robot navigation (LM-Nav, VLMaps, etc.) assumes static environments and never uses the agent's own experience, so it repeatedly repeats the same collisions with danger signs, people stepping out from walls, or doors that open unexpectedly.
motivation: Real environments are stochastic, so plans built only from LLM general knowledge can fail and need refinement from experience. RL and imitation learning need many interactions or extra data, so they cannot correct behavior immediately. Inspired by human emotion as a spatial homeostasis mechanism, the paper seeks a training-free, one-shot behavior correction from a single experience.
key_idea: Maintain a spatial grid map (E2Map) that stores visual-language features plus emotion parameters modeled as weighted Gaussians; after an event, LMM/LLM turn the experience into an emotion score that widens the Gaussians near the involved object, raising the planner's cost there and changing behavior in one shot.
insight: Making the map itself a continuous, updatable cost field (rather than a binary obstacle map) lets a single language-derived emotion score directly reshape planning without any parameter learning. In simulation the baselines (VLMaps 0/10 on all three dynamic scenarios, LM-Nav 0-1/10) kept colliding after previous collisions, whereas E2Map reached 9/10, showing that the experience-based update is what gives the gain, since all methods share the same planner and controller. Note there is no ablation of individual components (prompts, update rule).
method: E2Map construction: top-down grid map storing LSeg visual-language features per cell (built from RGB-D and poses, as in VLMaps) plus emotion parameters (covariance, weight) per occupied cell.
Emotion field: emotion E(x) is a weighted sum of 2D Gaussians over occupied cells, with weights initialized to 1/N_valid and only Gaussians above a threshold considered; used as a navigation cost.

Event descriptor: GPT-4o receives three images (before, at, and after the event, offset h) and a step-by-step prompt to describe each scene and then the whole event; the event trigger comes from the simulator or sensors.
Emotion evaluator: Llama3 with few-shot prompts scores upsetness (0-3) and guiltiness (0-3) with reasons; the sum is s_emo.

E2Map update: for the n cells related to the event object, the std is updated as sigma_new = sigma * v_k * log(s_emo/T) (Weber-Fechner-inspired, v is the agent's heading direction), and weights are rescaled by N(p)/N_new(p) so the emotion magnitude at the cell is preserved while its spatial extent grows.
Goal selector: Llama3 converts instructions into code calling goal APIs (go_to, go_left_of, go_between, etc.), which ground objects via CLIP text similarity against the map, with outlier clustering.
Planning and control: D* over the emotion cost map, MPPI control, 3D LiDAR localization; replan after every E2Map update.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (frozen, event descriptor); Llama3 (frozen, emotion evaluator and goal selector); LSeg + CLIP (pretrained, frozen)
setting.observation: RGB-D camera images, poses (GT in sim, LiDAR localization in real), 3D LiDAR
setting.action_space: Cost-map path planning (D*) with MPPI velocity control on a quadruped (Unitree Go1)
setting.privileged: Event occurrence is signaled by simulator/sensor info; ground-truth pose in simulation; initial map built beforehand

numbers.eval_set_note: 10 language instructions per scenario in a custom Gazebo environment
numbers.extra: success = reaching all goals in order without collisions; one-shot update from experience within episodes

numbers.eval_set_note: 10 trials per scenario, conference room with a Go1 robot; danger sign and human-wall
numbers.extra: real Unitree Go1; dynamic door excluded

numbers_note: Results are success counts out of 10 (converted to percent); no standard benchmark is used, and only a custom scenario set was evaluated.
results: In Gazebo, E2Map reaches 9/10 in danger sign, human-wall and dynamic door, versus VLMaps 0/10 on all three and LM-Nav 1/10, 0/10, 1/10. On the static setting E2Map and VLMaps get 10/10 and LM-Nav 5/10. Real-world results (9/10 in both tested scenarios) match simulation.
limitations: Event detection relies on simulator/sensor signals rather than an autonomous anomaly detector.
Experiments cover only negative emotions in a single small custom environment with 10 trials per scenario; positive emotions are shown only qualitatively.
No ablations and small sample size; baselines were adapted with a shared planner, and the initial collision is still required (one-shot means after the first failure).
